To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the existence of a pure strategy Nash equilibrium is guaranteed in games with a continuum of players and discontinuities in the payoff functions, provided the payoff functions are continuous in a security sense and the strategy spaces are compact.

(1) in games with a continuum of players, a pure strategy Nash equilibrium always exists when the security of the game is continuous and (2) the optimal income tax always exists in a large class of optimal income tax problems.

the game-theoretic results in Balder (2002) can be extended to games with discontinuous (and even non-measurable) payoff functions, and that these results can be used to establish the existence of optimal income taxes.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the presence of discontinuities in the payoff functions of a game with a measure space, the existence of a Nash equilibrium is guaranteed by imposing a mild continuity requirement on the security of a player.
the existence of Nash equilibrium in the game-theoretic model of Mirrleles (1971) is established without any convexity assumptions on the utility functions of the players.

, in the context of games with a continuum of players, we are able to extend to the discontinuous case the line of research initiated by Reny (1998) and continued in Reny (1992) and McLennan, Mordukhovich and Papageorgiou (2010) which, in the case of finite players, establishes the equivalence between the existence of Nash equilibrium and that of continuous security.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the existence of a Nash equilibrium in games in which the players are not allowed to randomize is a robust property, which is not affected by the presence of a measure space of (non-randomized) players and/or discontinuous payoff functions.
, in the context of games with a continuum of players, it is not necessary to assume the continuity of the payoff functions in order to guarantee the existence of a pure strategy Nash equilibrium.
our existence result is applicable in situations where the payoff functions are not necessarily continuous and the players' preferences are not necessarily continuous.
